Resolves #18788

The measured-row-height arm in `test/playwright/unit/list/animatePlugin.spec.mjs` asks about the `list.plugin.Animate` guard instead of about the whole process. It captured `console.error` and asserted *nothing* was logged, and one worker runs many spec files, so a wedge watchdog armed five seconds earlier by `functional/HtmlTemplateComponent.spec.mjs` failed it — four CI jobs across three branches today, none touching `list/`.

Evidence: L3 (the real unit tier, red-first and after, plus the paired run) → L3 required (the AC is suite behavior). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the PR body and file-size guards ran.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | Mutation: inverting the guard's `measureItemHeight` condition in `src/list/plugin/Animate.mjs:151` reds both guard arms (`a measured config draws no complaint`), and restoring it greens them — the arm still catches a guard that misbehaves |
| AC-2 | New arm *an error from elsewhere in the process does not decide this guard* emits a foreign wedge message inside the capture window: red with the unfiltered capture (`Expected - 1 / Received + 3`), green with the filter |
| AC-3 | `list/animatePlugin.spec.mjs` 25/25 |
| AC-4 | `animatePlugin.spec.mjs` + `functional/HtmlTemplateComponent.spec.mjs` in one worker: 30/30; the unit tier runs in this PR's CI |

## Deltas from ticket
- The capture moved into a small `captureGuardErrors(fn)` helper, so both assertions read the same filtered subject and the second arm can exercise exactly that path. The existing arm's two halves are otherwise unchanged in meaning.

## Test Evidence
- **Red-first:** with the helper written but the filter absent, the new foreign-error arm fails — that is the CI failure mode reproduced on demand, without needing a five-second timer to line up.
- **Mutation receipt for AC-1** as above; `src/list/plugin/Animate.mjs` restored byte-identical.
- **What this does not do:** the watchdog still fires and still logs for whoever owns the in-flight update. Whether a component leaves one behind is its own broadcast defect-note, not this leaf.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] The `unit` job stops reporting `animatePlugin.spec.mjs:551` as flaky across the next several CI runs on unrelated PRs.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** micro — one test file, one new arm and a helper extracted from the arm beside it; the narrowing is a scoping fix, not an architectural concept.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that the measured-row-height arm asks a process-wide question about a guard-local subject, and the diff narrows the subject without touching the question. Verified against the exact head `a366bfcfd0`, in a rig that runs these specs — my first attempt used a `/private/tmp` worktree with symlinked `node_modules`, which reds five unrelated `functional/HtmlTemplateComponent` arms on its own, so that was instrument rather than subject. The one thing I looked for and did not find: a filter narrow enough to go silently green. It filters on the class name rather than the message, so `Animate.mjs:152` (which carries both the token and `measureItemHeight`) and `:238` (`minItemWidth must be null or a positive finite px number`) are both admitted — the whitelist covers the guard family, not only the message under test. And the usual whitelist hazard is self-checked here: a renamed prefix would empty `refused` too, so `refused.some(… 'measureItemHeight')` reds in the same test rather than letting the first assertion pass vacuously. Mutation reproduced independently — `return captured` in place of the filter reds the new arm on the injected wedge message (`Received + 3`), and restoring it greens. Counts at that head: `animatePlugin` 25/25 with the new arm confirmed **by exact title**, because a filename-only run can report green while a new arm never matched; the pair with `functional/HtmlTemplateComponent.spec.mjs` on one worker 30/30; CI 20/20. Bounded repair holds — the only `console.error` capture under `test/playwright/unit/list/` is the one this patch replaces.

**Findings:** None. No required actions.
